subject: Follow-up: HIPAA scope — BAA availability & deployment options
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@medintegrity.com>, Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@medintegrity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: HIPAA scope — BAA availability & deployment options

Hi Hannah / Tom — thanks for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery and clear next asks so we can scope the right hosting option: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workload: ingesting patient EHR extracts (HL7/CCD) for normalization and summary generation; downstream clinicians will query summaries; some users will paste free-text clinical notes into the UI.
- Required protections: PHI processing in scope, audit logs, and customer-managed key option are preferred.
- Timeline: pilot in Q4 (sandbox), production in Q1.

Open questions / asks for you
1) BAA: confirm whether you require Redwood to sign a BAA for any pilot or just production. We can provide our standard BAA; if you need earlier legal redlines please flag critical clauses.
2) SOC 2: please confirm whether Type II within the last 12 months is required. We can share our latest SOC 2 report under NDA.
3) PHI boundaries: confirm whether PHI will ever be written to persistent storage outside the model response (e.g., logs, transcript store, S3). If yes, we need to map retention controls.
4) Deployment preference: you mentioned Dedicated vs Private VPC — can you confirm which you prefer for the pilot? Hosted API (shared) is not typically eligible for PHI by default; Dedicated or Private are the expected options.
5) Vendor questionnaire: if you have a security questionnaire (or an initial set of controls), please send it and we’ll complete the intake.

Next steps (from Redwood)
- I will send the vendor questionnaire and a short checklist mapping capabilities to your asks (SOC 2, BAA sample, KMS options).
- Marissa (SE) will handle technical details for Dedicated vs Private VPC and customer-managed key capabilities.
- We’ll propose a 30–40m technical follow-up next week to walk security/devops.

Attachments: none on this note (I’ll accept the questionnaire when you send it).

Thanks again — we can move quickly once we have the questionnaire + your confirmation on BAA timing.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@medintegrity.com>

Cc: Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@medintegrity.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 13:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: HIPAA scope — BAA availability & deployment options

Diego — thank you for the recap, that's helpful. Couple quick answers and I've attached our standard vendor security questionnaire for your intake team to complete.

Answers:
- BAA: We will need Redwood to sign a BAA before production. For the pilot, we can accept a short-term letter of intent but would like to see sample BAA language now.
- SOC 2: We require a SOC 2 Type II report covering the past 12 months. Please indicate whether you can share redacted evidence under NDA.
- PHI flow: For the pilot we expect EHR extracts (S3 transfer) + occasional clinician-pasted notes via UI. All PHI must be processed within your environment that meets BAA controls and must be deletable on request.
- Deployment: our preference for pilot is Dedicated capacity with customer key control; long-term may move to Private VPC depending on integration complexity.

Attachment: MedIntegrity_Vendor_Q_20270804.pdf (PDF, 18 pages) — questionnaire contains a short SOC/Security checklist and some specific KMS/QoS asks (Section 4).

Please have your security team complete sections 2–5 and return by EOD Friday so our compliance reviewers can triage.

Hannah Lee
CISO, MedIntegrity Health

Thanks — quick update from SE/security side: 

1) SOC 2: attaching our latest report (SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf). We can share this under a standard NDA; I'll start the NDA workflow now.
2) BAA: attaching our current sample BAA (Sample_BAA_Redwood_v1.2.pdf). Legal is OK with this as a starting point; if MedIntegrity flags anything specific we'll escalate.
3) Dedicated + KMS: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via our KMS integration today for Dedicated and Private VPC; for Dedicated there is a short onboarding (key provisioning & test encrypt/decrypt) that our infra team completes (2–3 business days). Private on-prem remains an option but adds integration overhead.
4) PHI flow & retention: we can map ingestion paths (S3 import pipeline + UI inputs). Logs by default are redacted for model inputs but we can enable full audit logging within Dedicated/Private environments and implement deletion on request.

Next step: Diego — can you propose 2 slots for a technical deep-dive next Tue/Wed? I will have the infra engineer and security SME on the call.
